purpose: Audio orchestration defaults shared by pycore (pyctl/audio_orchestration), the pycore-manager UI and the wordnew client composer (shared/orchestration). docs_fix/DESIGN_AUDIO_ORCHESTRATION.md, docs_fix/DESIGN_WORDNEW_CLIENT.md.

transfer.purpose: Clip transfer between pycore / Laravel and the clients. Many small clips move as framed bundles (one request, no per-file round trip): pycore ui/audio_orch/resource/bundle and Laravel /api/app_qy_v1/ai_tools/tts/audio/bundle answer the same frame. pycore also serves one clip raw (resource/file, GET); Laravel answers URL batches (sentence/audio/head, word/audio/head). Clients keep at most the per-backend parallel limit of transfers in flight (device setting, default parallel_defaults, 1..parallel_max); the native app writes bundle frames straight to disk.
transfer.pycore_bundle_frame: per request item, in order: 4-byte big-endian header length, UTF-8 JSON header {index, key, hit, bytes, sent, meaning}, then `bytes` payload bytes when sent is true (a hit past the byte budget is sent:false and is asked again)

book_plan.purpose: Server-owned audio plan of one book. The client posts the plan once (book, languages, reading position); Laravel derives the required clips from its own book data, raises their gap rows by reading position and keeps counters; the client follows by cursor and downloads only newly ready clips. Every node generates through work leases.

assignments_request.from: int: sentence seq the windows start at (the reader position)
assignments_request.windows: [{sid, lane, language, count}] in play order; sid is a work node's short id or direct_sid (the app's direct pycore); count = pending clips of that lane and language the node takes, laid out one after another from `from`, per lane and language independently

book_plan.assignments_rule: App-led scheduling. While the app is open it computes the windows from the roster it knows (Laravel nodes with lanes, class and throughput, plus its direct pycore) and POSTs them; each POST is the plan heartbeat. Laravel resolves every window to a position range of the plan's pending clips and, for assignment_ttl_seconds after the last POST, leases a window's rows only to its node (the node claims them first, every other node's claim skips them; direct_sid windows are skipped by all nodes: the direct pycore generates them). When the heartbeat expires (the app closed) the ranges are dropped and the claims fall back to Laravel's own fair share. Ranges are re-laid out on a changed window set, a reader move of reprioritize_min_move or every assignment_relayout_seconds.
book_plan.assignments_response: {fresh, expires_in, windows: [{sid, lane, assigned, generating, done}]}: per node and lane, summed over languages; assigned and done are cumulative over the plan (relayouts carry finished clips), generating is the live leases inside the node's current ranges. The app sizes a window as the node's items per hour x assignment_horizon_minutes (at least assignment_min_clips)

plan_request.languages: sentence languages the plan voices (iso codes)
plan_request.include_words: bool: also the distinct words of the primary-language sentences
plan_request.position: int: sentence seq the reader is at (priority is raised from there forward)
plan_request.plan_hash: client plan hash (idempotence marker, at most 64 chars)

status_response.generating: int clips under a live lease
status_response.failed: int clips whose retry budget ran out
status_response.ready_cursor: int, the highest ready sequence handed out (0 = none)
status_response.nodes: [{sid, label, platform, compute_class, count}] clips of the plan each node generates now
status_response.assignments: assignments_response of the plan (fresh false when no app heartbeat is live)
status_response.fast_pass: bool: the plan runs its sentence fast pass
status_response.upgrade: {total, done}: fast-pass sentences and those already upgraded by the quality pass

ready_response.ids: [resource id] ready clips after the cursor (sha256 resource ids, ready sequence order)
ready_response.cursor: int, pass it as the next request's cursor

fast_pass.rule: DISABLED (enabled=false): sentences are accepted only from the quality-floor engine (queue_center_contract work_leases.sentence_quality). When enabled, a plan whose missing sentences exceed missing_threshold runs the fast pass: any node whose sentence lane declares the fast engine (cpu or gpu, Colab-CPU included) may lease that plan's sentence rows with engine_hint = engine and delivers the base clip; once delivered, a gpu node whose lane declares quality_engine may lease the row again as an upgrade (variant_key = quality_variant, engine_hint = quality_engine) and delivers the quality variant next to the base clip. Clients play the clip that is ready: the quality variant when the server holds it, else the base.

step_options.meaning: word steps only: after each word, read its short Chinese meaning (wordnew implements it; pycore: open item in docs_fix/DESIGN_AUDIO_ORCHESTRATION.md)
